questions.contextText:
Reading Comprehension (Q.46 – Q.50): Read the following passage carefully and answer the
questions that follow.
The revival of millets—often termed 'nutri-cereals'—marks a significant shift in contemporary
agricultural policy toward climate resilience and nutritional security. Unlike water-intensive crops
such as paddy and sugarcane, millets thrive in arid and semi-arid soils with minimal irrigation and
synthetic inputs. Historically a staple across rain-fed regions of India, millets gradually lost ground
to polished rice and wheat following the Green Revolution's emphasis on high-yielding varieties and
public procurement. Today, targeted state missions are reintroducing millets into public distribution
systems and school midday meals, simultaneously boosting farmer incomes in tribal belts and
combating widespread micronutrient deficiencies.
questions.questionText: Why are millets considered suitable for climate-resilient agriculture?
options: They grow well in dry soils with minimal water and inputs
They can only be cultivated in flooded fields
They mature faster than all vegetables

'ମହୌଷଧି' ଶବ୍ଦର ସନ୍ଧି ବିଚ୍ଛେଦ କ'ଣ?

'ଷଡ଼୍‌ଯନ୍ତ୍ର' ଶବ୍ଦର ସନ୍ଧି ବିଚ୍ଛେଦ କ'ଣ?
